design_name: Rheum-Bract Stratified Glazing (double-pane window with low-conductivity gas cavity and warm-edge spacer)
inspiration_source: Rheum nobile (Himalayan 'glasshouse plant'): translucent, overlapping bracts that enclose a still-air chamber around the inflorescence, keeping internal temperatures up to ~10 K above ambient at high altitude; secondary analog: stratified, still-air insulation of snowpack
physical_mechanism: Semantic features of the request: steady conduction through a layered solid-gas-solid stack, a large thermal-conductivity contrast (glass k~1 W/m/K vs. gas k~0.02 W/m/K), convective (Robin) exchange with warm indoor and cold outdoor air, and a 2D edge effect where the spacer/frame bridges the cavity. The cross-domain analog is Rheum nobile, whose thin translucent bracts trap a thin, still air layer between tissue sheets: the bract sheets themselves conduct well, but the trapped gas layer, kept thin enough to suppress buoyant convection (low Rayleigh number), carries most of the thermal resistance. Translated to the window: two thin glass panes (the 'bracts') enclose a narrow argon-filled cavity whose width is chosen near the convection-onset optimum (~12-16 mm), so the gas behaves as a nearly pure conductor with an effective conductivity only slightly above molecular. The temperature field is modeled by 2D steady conduction, div(k(x,y) grad T) = 0, over a vertical cross-section (thickness x height), with piecewise-constant k (glass / gas / glass), Robin conditions h_in(T_in - T) and h_out(T - T_out) on the room- and exterior-facing surfaces, and adiabatic top/bottom edges (or a conductive spacer strip to capture the edge-of-glass cold bridge). Expected result: almost all of the ~20 K indoor-outdoor drop occurs across the gas cavity and the surface films; each glass pane has only a ~0.1-0.2 K drop; inner-surface temperature stays around 13-15 C, well above the room-air dew point, which is the practical design criterion (condensation and comfort).

parameters.name: glass_thickness
parameters.justification: Standard float glass pane thickness 4 mm (3-10 mm commercially); analog of the thin, conductive bract sheet.

parameters.name: gap_width
parameters.justification: Gas cavity width; 12 mm is typical, optimum for argon near 12-16 mm before convection cells form (Ra-limited), analogous to the thin still-air layer between Rheum bracts.

parameters.name: window_height
parameters.justification: Vertical extent of the modeled cross-section (2D domain height).

parameters.name: glass_conductivity
parameters.justification: Soda-lime float glass thermal conductivity ~1.0 W/(m K).

parameters.name: gas_conductivity
parameters.justification: Argon fill ~0.017-0.018 W/(m K) at ~0 C; air is ~0.024-0.026. Effective value assumes convection is suppressed (narrow gap).

parameters.name: indoor_temperature
parameters.justification: Indoor air 20 C (K), typical winter setpoint.

parameters.name: outdoor_temperature
parameters.justification: Outdoor air -10 C (K), typical winter design condition (range -30 to +5 C).

parameters.name: h_inside
parameters.justification: Combined natural-convection + radiation film coefficient on the indoor surface, W/(m^2 K) (EN 673 uses ~7.7).

parameters.name: h_outside
parameters.justification: Wind-driven exterior film coefficient, W/(m^2 K) (EN 673 uses 25).

parameters.name: spacer_conductivity
parameters.justification: Edge spacer conductivity: warm-edge polymer composite ~0.2-0.3 W/(m K) vs. aluminum ~160; controls the 2D edge-of-glass cold bridge.
